problem: Navigation foundation models (e.g. NoMaD) fail on novel camera configurations (fisheye-like pre-training vs pinhole deployment), with poor geometric perception and obstacle avoidance. Full fine-tuning and naive RGB-D early fusion on small in-domain data cause catastrophic forgetting and less diverse trajectories.
motivation: NFMs are RGB-only, so domain shifts in camera geometry and scene layout impair distance estimation and clearance. Fine-tuning is needed to calibrate them, but it erodes the pre-trained prior. The authors want to add geometry awareness without destroying pre-trained behaviors.
key_idea: Attach a trainable depth-conditioned copy of the frozen NoMaD backbone via ControlNet-style zero-initialized 1x1 conv residual pathways, so dense depth is injected without disturbing the pre-trained policy.
insight: Zero-initialized residual injection preserves the prior at initialization and learns geometry gradually. Full fine-tuning (NoMaD-FT) and early-fusion RGB-D (NoMaD-EF) both fall below zero-shot NoMaD on several offline datasets and real-world scenarios, which the authors attribute to forgetting. D-CLING matches or beats zero-shot on the original NoMaD datasets, and the RGB-only variant of D-CLING scores far lower on Multi Obstacle (10 vs 100), showing depth matters, especially out of distribution.
method: Frozen RGB Branch: the pre-trained NoMaD (ViNT encoders + transformer + U-Net diffusion head) with all weights frozen.
Depth Branch: a trainable copy of NoMaD taking RGB-D (4-channel input) through a 4->3 embedding layer, otherwise same architecture.
Zero-init residual injection: zero-initialized 1x1 convs before the U-Net and after each U-Net stage of the depth branch; the output is added element-wise to the RGB branch, y'_l = y_l + Z_l(u_l^d).
Training: unmodified NoMaD diffusion loss, AdamW with cosine schedule, 30 epochs, batch 256, lr 2.5e-5, single RTX 4090, on the 3 h RealHSRNav dataset.
Depth source: a learned stereo-to-depth estimator (ZED 2) on the real robot; Depth-Anything V2 to synthesize depth for the NoMaD datasets in offline evaluation.

setting.backbone: NoMaD (ViNT-based transformer + diffusion U-Net), frozen RGB branch + trainable depth-branch copy
setting.training_data: Pre-trained NoMaD checkpoint; fine-tuned only on RealHSRNav (~3 h of RGB-odometry demonstrations from a Toyota HSR in an office)
setting.observation: RGB history (T+1=4 frames) + estimated dense depth per frame + goal image (topological map of goal images)
setting.action_space: H+1=8 predicted 2-D waypoints in the robot frame (diffusion-sampled); linear speed limited to 0.45 m/s, angular to 1.0 rad/s
setting.simulator: real world only (plus offline dataset evaluation)
setting.privileged: none (pre-collected goal images of the route as topological map)

results: D-CLING gets 70% / 60% SR on Basic Obstacle / Dynamic Corridor and 1.2 interventions on the long route, beating zero-shot NoMaD (50 / 0 / 2.6), NoMaD-FT (30 / 10 / 3.2) and NoMaD-EF (40 / 0 / 4.4). Offline, it has the lowest error on the fine-tuning dataset and is competitive with or better than zero-shot NoMaD on the pre-training datasets, unlike FT/EF.
limitations: Only NoMaD was tested; generality to other NFMs is unverified.
Limited temporal context (4 frames, no memory) causes re-collisions after avoiding an obstacle that has moved off-screen.
Small real-world trial counts (5-10) and a single office environment; depends on an estimated depth model, and offline depth for the NoMaD datasets is synthesized.
